summary: You were in the hospital with a bad kidney infection. A stone was blocking the tube from your kidney, so the doctors put in a small tube called a stent. You are going home with an antibiotic and a pill that helps with the stent. Finish the antibiotic and drink enough water. Keep your urology visit so the stone and the stent can be taken care of.

diagnoses.plain: A serious infection that started in the urinary tract and spread to the blood (sepsis)
diagnoses.clinical: Sepsis due to complicated urinary tract infection

diagnoses.plain: A kidney stone blocking the tube from the left kidney, causing swelling
A small tube (stent) was placed to let the urine drain
Kidneys were strained for a short time, now back to normal

new.name: Cefpodoxime
new.howOften: twice a day by mouth for 7 more days
new.why: An antibiotic to finish treating the infection. Take every dose even if you feel better.

new.name: Tamsulosin
new.howOften: once a day by mouth while the stent is in place
new.why: Relaxes the urine tube so the stent is more comfortable. Keep taking it unless urology tells you to stop.

new.name: Acetaminophen
new.howOften: as needed for mild pain or fever, within the daily limit your care team gave you

continue.name: Atorvastatin
continue.why: Lowers cholesterol to protect your heart.

continue.name: Home diabetes medications
continue.howOften: as on your final medication list

stop.name: Lisinopril
stop.why: On hold until your doctor rechecks your kidneys and blood pressure. Do not restart it on your own.

stop.name: NSAIDs
stop.why: Avoid pain relievers like ibuprofen. They can hurt your kidneys after this illness. Ask first.

checklist.text: Take Cefpodoxime 200 mg twice a day until it is gone
Take Tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day while the stent is in
Keep lisinopril on hold until your doctor says otherwise
See urology to plan stone treatment and stent removal. The stent cannot stay in forever
Get your kidney function rechecked as directed
Check your blood sugar as your diabetes plan says
Drink plenty of water unless a doctor told you to limit fluids

call911: Confusion, fainting, severe weakness, or trouble breathing
goToER: Worsening pain in your side or belly
Vomiting that will not stop or you cannot keep your medicines down
Making much less urine than usual
Signs the blockage or infection is back
callClinic: Questions about stent symptoms such as a frequent urge to urinate or mild discomfort

followUps.why: Treat the stone and remove or exchange the stent
Recheck your kidney function and blood pressure, and decide about lisinopril

questionsToAsk: When is my urology appointment, and who do I call to schedule it?
What stent symptoms are normal and which ones mean infection?
How much acetaminophen can I take in one day?
When should my kidney blood test be done?
